messages.400.art-label: A puzzle piece hovering askew above its socket, not fitting
messages.400.description: The server couldn't understand this request (400 Bad Request) — the link may be incomplete, a parameter malformed, or the page state may have expired.
messages.400.hint-1: Check that the link in the address bar is complete
messages.400.hint-2: Refresh the page for a clean state
messages.400.hint-3: Start over from the home page and repeat the action
messages.400.title: This request doesn't fit together
messages.403.art-label: A closed door with a padlock on it
messages.403.description: Your current identity doesn't have access to this page (403 Forbidden). It may be admin-only, or outside the scope of your invite link.
messages.403.hint-1: If you're the administrator, sign in first
messages.403.hint-2: If you arrived via an invite link, ask the inviter about its scope
messages.403.hint-3: Head back home, to places you can access
messages.403.title: This door isn't open to you right now
messages.404.art-label: A map whose dotted path ends in a cross
messages.404.description: The page you're looking for doesn't exist (404 Not Found) — it may have been moved or deleted, or the address may simply have one letter too many.
messages.404.hint-2: Go back home and find it again from the navigation
messages.404.hint-3: If it should exist (say, a feature page went missing), tell us on GitHub
messages.404.title: This place may once have existed
messages.429.art-label: An hourglass with sand still falling
messages.429.description: Your requests came in too fast and hit the rate limit (429 Too Many Requests). This isn't a ban — just a short pause, and everything works again afterwards.
messages.429.hint-1: Wait about half a minute, then refresh or retry
messages.429.hint-2: Reduce the number of open pages and concurrent actions
messages.429.title: Slow down and take a breath
messages.4xx.description: The request couldn't be accepted (a 4xx client error). The exact cause depends on the request itself — its format, permissions, rate, or the state of the target resource.
messages.4xx.hint-1: Check that your input and the link are correct
messages.4xx.hint-2: Refresh the page and repeat the action
messages.4xx.hint-3: Go back home and start again from a normal entry point
messages.4xx.title: Something went wrong on the request side
messages.500.art-label: A server lying down for a nap
messages.500.description: The server hit an unexpected internal error while handling the request (500 Internal Server Error). The request didn't complete, but your data wasn't harmed.
messages.500.hint-1: Wait a moment, then try again
messages.500.hint-2: If it keeps happening, open the log files (the log directory) for the actual exception
messages.500.hint-3: Bring the error from the logs to a GitHub issue and we'll fix it
messages.500.title: It's not your fault — maybe the server is tired
messages.502.art-label: A broken bridge with a cloud on the far side
messages.502.description: The server received an invalid response from an upstream service (such as Pixiv) while forwarding the request (502 Bad Gateway). The problem is most likely upstream or in the network path — not your device.
messages.502.hint-1: Wait a moment and retry; upstream may just be briefly unstable
messages.502.hint-2: Check that your proxy and network connection are working
messages.502.hint-3: Make sure your Pixiv cookie is still valid; save a fresh one if it expired
messages.502.title: The other end of the bridge isn't answering
messages.503.art-label: A cup of coffee with rising steam
messages.503.description: The service is temporarily unavailable (503 Service Unavailable) — it may be under maintenance, restarting, or briefly overloaded. It usually recovers within tens of seconds.
messages.503.hint-2: If it doesn't recover for a long time, check the logs or report it on GitHub
messages.503.title: Taking a short break — back soon
messages.5xx.description: The server encountered an error while handling the request (a 5xx server error). This wasn't caused by anything you did — the problem is on our side.
messages.5xx.hint-1: Wait a moment, then try again
messages.5xx.hint-2: If it keeps happening, open the log files (the log directory) for the actual exception
messages.5xx.hint-3: Bring the symptoms and logs to a GitHub issue and we'll fix it
messages.5xx.title: Something went wrong on the server side
